rationale: 'Mechanical classification directly maps to the Mechanical Team handling rotating equipment.'
'Electrical motor fault maps to Electrical Team.'

A hot-running compressor can superficially resemble a motor-temperature issue. The compressor asset context together with cooling failure and contamination evidence indicate a machine cooling problem rather than an electrical supply fault.

The robotic-arm asset can suggest a mechanical problem, but over-travel past a home limit is governed by position sensing and control feedback. The limit-switch symptom and sensor failure evidence outweigh the arm mechanism.

Erratic SCADA flow values conflict with a physically steady cooling-water flow. The flow-meter asset and disagreement between indication and process condition localize the issue to measurement or control rather than water-moving equipment.

Pressure loss on a press could be interpreted as a reading problem, but reduced tonnage under load and a suspected seal leak point to the hydraulic power path. The press asset and load-dependent symptom distinguish it from an instrument fault.
